summary: Unexpected model handoff from pinned session during abbreviated health window
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary rollout for EchoDrive on us-west production, a subset of tenant sessions that were explicitly pinned to redwood-open-1.1 were observed to be serviced by the fallback variant (rw-v1-quant). The switch coincided with a transient increase in healthcheck frequency caused by a control-plane probe backoff shorten during a hotpath patch. The handoff removed per-session pin affinity for ~7s for some connections and led to content-quality regressions reported by the customer.

Impact:
- ~3% of EchoDrive production requests for the rollout cohort returned responses from rw-v1-quant instead of the pinned redwood-open-1.1 variant.
- Customer reported reduced generation quality and higher token hallucination rate in affected requests.
- No 5xx errors or user-visible timeouts; mostly scoring/quality regressions.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (EchoDrive) in us-west on Redwood Dedicated cluster pool-echo-03.
- Canary rollout weight: 8% cohort.
- Canary healthcheck window configured with aggressive probe policy (0.5s probes during short backoff).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Canary weight increase applied at 2026-03-10T15:12:00Z via rollout API.
2) Control plane applied shortened health backoff patch at 2026-03-10T15:12:07Z to mitigate probe backlog.
3) Between 15:12:08Z and 15:12:15Z a subset of edge connections lost pin affinity and were routed to fallback variant.
4) Traffic returned to normal after ~9s without operator intervention.

Logs / evidence:
- Edge proxy logs (edge-usw-21) show pin-cookie TTL refresh suppressed and an immediate route recalculation at 15:12:08Z. (link: logs.redwood.ai/echo/edge-usw-21/2026-03-10/15:12)
- Orchestrator trace shows PreemptiveFallbackDecision triggered due to perceived unhealthy canary slice at 15:12:07Z (trace id: 7f2a1b6c).
- Serving runtime metrics: KVCache hit-rate unchanged; latency stable; but variant selection histogram shows spike to rw-v1-quant.

Initial hypothesis:
- The control-plane's temporary modification to healthcheck backoff shortened the probe cadence and tripped a preemptive fallback heuristic which incorrectly invalidated per-session pin leases before the orchestrator could commit a renewed pin. Edge cookie refresh race with the probe caused the session to miss renewal and be considered eligible for fallback.

Immediate customer communication:
- Notified EchoDrive CSM and engineering at 2026-03-10T16:00Z. Provided temporary mitigation suggestion to pause canary weight changes until healthbackoff patch reverted.

Desired outcome:
- Prevent transient health-probe cadence changes from causing pin lease invalidations. Ensure pins are sticky across short-lived control-plane probe policy windows.
investigation_notes:
Investigators: Liam O'Connor (SRE), Priya Raman (Serving).
Findings so far:
- The orchestrator's PreemptiveFallbackDecision consults a health-window accumulator that uses a probe-rate-derived threshold; when probe cadence increases, short windows can cross the unhealthy threshold quickly.
- Pin leases are renewed by the edge cookie refresh TTL path; during the probe cadence spike the cookie refresh RPCs were deprioritized behind health probes in the edge event loop, causing ~12% of active session renewals to be delayed beyond the lease expiry micro-window.
- No model eviction or GPU shortage observed.
- Reproduced in staging by simulating health backoff shorten while driving sustained connection churn; observed identical transient unpin and fallback.

Next investigative steps:
- Add synthetic test in precommit suite that simulates probe cadence shifts and measures pin coherence under load.
- Evaluate quick fix: guard PreemptiveFallbackDecision to ignore transient windows < 10s when session pins exist.
- Long term: separate pin-lease renewal from probe-priority queue and add explicit hysteresis in fallback decision logic.

resolution:
Workaround: paused canary weight changes by EchoDrive and deployed orchestrator gating rule that prevents PreemptiveFallbackDecision from invalidating pin leases when unhealthy windows are <10s and there are active pinned sessions.

Permanent fix planned: separate pin-lease renewal path from health-probe event queue and add explicit 10s hysteresis to fallback decision. Add synthetic test cases and an integration test for pin coherence across rapid probe cadence changes.

Status: Mitigation applied in us-west and monitoring indicates no further occurrences for EchoDrive. Permanent work slated in SRE backlog and tracked under INT-3312 (orchestrator-pin-hysteresis epic).
